chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Kazzaz from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father from Ali (peace be upon him): In

If a man married a woman and found her to have leprosy or a cleft palate, he said: 'If he has not yet consummated the marriage and no option has been presented to him, then if he wishes he may divorce her, and if he wishes he may keep her, and she is entitled to her dowry (sadaq). And if he consummates the marriage with her, then she is his wife.' This does not contradict the first report which included that she is returned without divorce, because his saying (peace be upon him) 'if he wishes he divorces' is interpreted as 'if he wishes he releases her,' because that is derived from it in the root of the language, and it was not carried upon the established divorce in the law. As for his saying 'if he consummates with her, then she is his wife,' its meaning is: if he consummates with her while knowing of that condition, then he will not have the right to return her afterwards in any state, because that indicates his satisfaction with her condition in that state, as we will clarify later.

key_terms.بَرْصَاءَ: A woman with leprosy or a skin disease
key_terms.جَذْمَاءَ: A woman with a cleft palate

ai.seo_question: What are the rights and options of a husband who discovers his wife has a physical defect after marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *al-tadlis* (concealment of defects) in marriage, establishing that pre-consummation allows for a discretionary choice (*ikhtiyar*) to either divorce or retain the wife without financial penalty, whereas post-consummation renders the marriage binding. Shia scholars interpret the phrase 'if he wishes, he divorces' as implying the right to separate (*khal'a*) rather than strictly requiring a formal *talaq*, highlighting the flexibility in resolving such disputes before the marital bond is fully sealed. This ruling underscores the principle of consent and transparency, ensuring that a spouse is not bound to a partner with undisclosed physical ailments once the marriage is consummated.
